newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Lower-than-expected U.S. inflation figures jolted South African markets, reversing bullion's shortlived revival and trimming almost three percent off the gold share index. Bonds were boosted to their firmest levels since October.
- Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau has stepped in again and squashed Transnet's unauthorised attempt to sell off its loss-makng cellular phone division.

- Development Bank loans to its borrowers -- mainly local governments and public utilities -- will be significantly more expensive in future following a decision by the bank to overhaul its interest rate policy.
- Nationwide Air has become the second independent domestic carrier in South Africa to negotiate a cooperative agreement with a major foreign operation, Belgian flag carrier Sabena.

- President Nelson Mandela and senior African National Congress members leave on Thursday for a four-day meeting at a secret venue where ther party will plan a two-year programme, which will largely focus on job creation.
- Only one local company has applied for tax holiday status and the government's lure to attract foreign investment has yet to be realised, a spokesman for the department of trade and industry said.

- Small manufacturers in the clothing industry are demanding a legal code of conduct as protection against some large retailers after the pre-Christmas closure of Miba Clothing, a small cut and trim operation in Durban.
- The Mine Health and Safety Act, which tightens regulations governing South Africa's accident-prone mining industry, came into effect on Wednesday.
- Gold bounced wildly on international markets on Wednesday as traders watched the precious metal gain $2 and then rapidly fall back again.
- President Nelson Mandela lashed out at the United States for its attempts to block South Africa's arm sales to Syria.
- An angry South African entertainer has accused the police of bungling by arresting his younger brother as a robbery suspect following the rapes of two sisters in Johannesburg.
